=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node, visible in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, forming a terminal cluster)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no visible teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapers to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapering to a narrow base, wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein with lateral veins branching off on each side)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins clearly visible, running parallel to each other, close together)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, glabrous (smooth surface with a glossy appearance)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, not noticeably elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, soft, and flexible, typical of young seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (bright green, consistent across images)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible upon stem breakage or damage)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen bases at leaf petiole attachment points)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves forming tendrils)

F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled arrangement of simple, elliptic leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. The stem is green, herbaceous, and smooth. Some leaves show minor damage (small holes present), but no signs of herbivory or pathogens are inferred. The plant is growing in a litter-covered forest floor environment, surrounded by rocks and fallen branches. Multiple images confirm the same individual from different angles, with consistent morphology.
